section.title: Teams
section.para: A team is a named group of users that an issue can be assigned to. Teams are created and filled in Manage > Teams. They belong to no project, and a user can be in any number of them. A team does not give its members access to anything: who can see and change an issue is still what the access levels of the project say.

The team of an issue is kept next to its handler, not instead of it: an issue can be assigned to a team before anybody has taken it on, and keeps the team when someone does. It is set with the Team field of the report and update pages, with the bulk action Assign Team of the issue list, or in the REST API ("team": {"id": 3} or {"name": "Support"}), by users who can assign issues ($g_update_bug_assign_threshold). It is shown to the users who can see who an issue is assigned to ($g_view_handler_threshold). The issue list can be filtered by team ([my teams] is the teams of the user) and has a sortable Team column, and the team box of My View lists the unresolved issues of the teams of the user. The members of the team of an issue are sent what is mailed about it, see the notify flag team.

listitem.para: Whether to enable teams. It defaults to OFF. Without it there is no Teams page, and no team on the issue pages, in the filter, in the columns of the issue list or in its bulk actions. Issues that were assigned to a team keep it while teams are off.
The access level needed to manage teams: create them, change them, delete them and put users in them. The default is ADMINISTRATOR.
